prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT (Target Off Block Time) issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded. Surface constraints are tactical capacity inputs, correlated with flight intent, stand and runway plan. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; forecasts from Flight Intent Message; arrival regulation when demand exceeds AAR, Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; AAR per runway config; recalculates on config/weather/staffing/sector change; persistent surface constraints become stand throughput/turn buffers/taxi-out); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT, Calculated Takeoff Time; Ground Delay Program; Pushback Window Token); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; TOBT protecting CTT; CTT to TSM; pushback spacing to Slot Allocation Engine); North and South Runway Meters (cut release rate near queue threshold; South preserves arrival separation); Surface Surveillance Adapter (status to Ramp Movement Board, TSM); Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display highlights surface advisories with stands, taxi segments, meters, flights; shows gate conflicts with flights, connection exposure, size compatibility, latest off-block time); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; uses Fuel Truck Hold Advice); Gate Conflict Detector (Gate Reopening Memo; resequences adjacent stands before broader delay; compares arrivals, departures, gates, towing, stand status); Airline Interface Adapter (Late Baggage Tag List); Handling Resource Planner (tests if extra handling beats flow measure); Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; Tactical Regulation Proposal; MUST distribute surface advisories within Business Rules Registry latency); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; Fuel Truck Hold Advice; apron advisories; MUST refresh apron layer within 5 s; stand timeline occupied/blocked/cleaning/boarding/tow-ready); Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger (MUST record every accepted surface/fuel/metering/apron adjustment with actor, timestamp, flight, rationale); Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Integrated Tactical Management Position; Sector Load Monitor; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Business Rules Registry; Identity Access Service; Digital Briefing Room. Modes (Airport Duty Manager declares): Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode (surface advisories weighted higher), Capacity Reduction

New part:
S474: The Surface Surveillance Adapter verifies that the apron position is physically clear, while the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor provide supporting movement evidence for the reopened area.
S475: The Tower Supervisor is advised only when the gate or stand decision changes runway sequence assumptions, expected taxi duration, or a departure metering commitment.
S476: The Aircraft Operator Representative confirms whether the aircraft can accept a revised stand assignment without disrupting maintenance release, fueling sequence, boarding control, or cabin readiness.
S477: The Handling Resource Planner estimates whether the proposed turnaround can be recovered using available loading teams, passenger stairs, boarding bridges, cleaning crews, and baggage transfer resources.
S478: The Airline Interface Adapter maintains airline-provided connection exposure, including protected passengers, minimum connection time pressure, and groups that require assisted transfer.
S479: The Regional Flow Manager balances passenger connection pressure against network fairness when a gate recovery action would improve one bank of departures but consume scarce apron capacity.
S480: The Network Operations Liaison reviews whether protecting a connecting passenger group supports wider network recovery or only transfers delay to a later sector.
S481: The Slot Coordinator protects constrained rotations by checking that a recovered gate plan remains compatible with the applicable Calculated Takeoff Time and any slot compliance expectation.
S482: The Target Off Block Time is revised only when the actor responsible for the turnaround confirms that the boarding, servicing, and ramp movement assumptions are achievable.
S483: The Departure Metering Service sequences recovered departures so that aircraft released from delayed turnarounds do not create a new surface queue at the runway holding points.
S484: Sector Load Monitor produces the Departure Fix Load Sheet when projected recovered departures require a consolidated view of demand by departure fix.
S485: The Airport CDM Portal shows downstream departure-fix pressure as contextual information for gate recovery decisions, without allowing the stand plan to override accepted airspace constraints.
S486: The Business Rules Registry holds the local rules for connection protection, gate compatibility, towing priority, stand reopening approval, and minimum turnaround recovery margins.
S487: The Collaborative Decision Log records each accepted conflict resolution with the chosen stand, rejected alternatives, affected passenger connections, and the rationale used by the responsible actor.
S488: The Audit Event Ledger preserves the same decision history for later traceability, including manual overrides, timestamp corrections, and identity of the approving role.
S489: The Performance Analytics Warehouse measures whether recovered gate assignments reduced missed connections, reduced secondary stand conflicts, and improved aircraft rotation stability during the Recovery Phase.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
